titel: What makes Michael Mann’s Collateral one of the best LA set films?

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts

einzeiler: A look back at Michael Mann's Los Angeles thriller Collateral with its stars and critics.
kurzfassung: The hosts and critics discuss Michael Mann's thriller Collateral following a special screening in Southern California. Actor Barry Shabaka Henley shares behind-the-scenes stories about working with the director and his co-stars. The panel analyzes the film's authentic portrayal of Los Angeles and its pioneering use of digital cinematography.
stichpunkte: Barry Shabaka Henley shares memories from filming his pivotal jazz club scene over three grueling nights.
The production originally considered Jack Black and Johnny Depp with a different director before Michael Mann took over.
Michael Mann completely changed Henley's musical performance and instrument right before shooting began.
The film was originally written to take place in New York with different directors and actors attached.
Shooting digitally on the Viper camera allowed the production to capture natural sodium lighting true to Los Angeles.
The movie showcases diverse neighborhoods and industrial areas of Los Angeles rarely seen on screen.
Tom Cruise and Jamie Foxx deliver standout performances, though only Foxx received an Oscar nomination.
Michael Mann utilizes numerous takes and close-ups to bypass acting technique and capture human truth.

kapitel.titel: Introduction and Barry Shabaka Henley's Casting

clips.hook: Steven Spielberg helped clear the actor's schedule for the role
clips.text: The actor explains how Steven Spielberg facilitated his release from another project, and mentions that the production was initially slated for a different filmmaker with entirely different lead actors.

clips.hook: A sudden direction change right before rolling cameras
clips.text: The performer describes being hit with major creative changes to the musical elements of his scene on the exact night of the shoot.

clips.hook: A completely different city and cast were originally planned
clips.text: The conversation reveals that the project was originally developed for a different East Coast metropolis with major comedy stars lined up for the lead roles.

clips.hook: The specific camera choice that captured the look of the city
clips.text: The critics analyze how utilizing an early digital camera technology allowed the production to authentically preserve nighttime urban lighting without artificial enhancements.

clips.hook: Pushing actors past exhaustion to find genuine human emotion
clips.text: The cast member details the director's intense shooting method involving dozens of takes designed to wear down traditional performance habits and expose raw reality.

beschreibung:
The topic:
For our most recent FilmWeek screening, Larry Mantle and critics Tim Cogshell and Claudia Puig traveled down to Santa Ana to the Frida Cinema for Michael Mann’s 2004 neo-noir thriller Collateral. The critics, along with special guest Barry Shabaka Henley, who plays the jazz club owner Daniel in the film, discuss the movie’s impact, its portrayal of Los Angeles, and the great acting by co-leads Jamie Foxx and a rare villainous Tom Cruise.
The panel:
Tim Cogshell, film critic for LAist, Alt-Film Guide and CineGods.com
Claudia Puig, film critic for LAist and program director for the Santa Barbara International Film Festival
Barry Shabaka Henley, film and television actor who plays the character Daniel in Collateral
